annotations.title: Look up a Kingdom Protocol object

description: Resolve any Living Bread lb: URN to its raw public JSON object. Protocol kinds (lb:gathering:<uuid>, lb:church:<uuid>, lb:ministry:<slug>, lb:community:<uuid>, lb:need:<uuid>, lb:service:<uuid>, lb:testimony:<uuid>, lb:prayer:<uuid>, lb:profile:<handle>) are read from the Kingdom Protocol v0.1 with their JSON Schema; any other lb: URN (directory church, city, Scripture, topic, biblical person) is resolved live through the public Kingdom Graph. Use when you hold a URN and need the machine-readable object. For a readable summary of a search result use fetch; for a directory church's full record use church. A private or unknown object returns found false, not an error; a string that is not an lb: URN also returns found false with the expected format. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.
name: kingdom_protocol_lookup

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

door.description: Documentation page for the protocol or graph.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

found.description: False when unknown, not public, or not a URN.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

object.description: The public object as stored, or null.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

protocol_kind.description: Protocol kind (gathering, church, ministry, community, need, service-opportunity, testimony, prayer, person), or null for Kingdom Graph entities.

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

schema.description: URL of the JSON Schema for this kind, or null.

source.description: The read that answered (a protocol function name, or kingdom_graph).

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: Look up a Kingdom Protocol object
